thread:
sam-support: FYI customer 'GreenLeaf Nonprofit' (acct GL-4421) says we charged MA sales tax on their March invoice even though they submitted a resale/exempt cert during signup.
laura-ops: Ugh, invoice 2026-03-11-GL4421? Can you paste the invoice link and the tax line?
sam-support: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/2026-03-11-GL4421 — tax line shows 'Massachusetts 6.25% local + 2.25% state = 8.5%'. They included exemption ID EX-993 in account fields and attached PDF in the support ticket.
fin-ellen: Thanks. Do we have a cached customer tax profile? sometimes our tax engine falls back to card BIN for jurisdiction.
girish-eng: Tagging in. I pulled the invoice-level payload from the invoice service:

```
{ "customer_id": "GL-4421", "billing_address": {"city": "Boston", "state": "MA"}, "payment_method": {"type": "card", "bin": "423456"}, "tax_jurisdiction": "MA", "tax_rate": 0.085 }
```

Looks normal. But our jurisdiction resolver returns granularity based on card BIN only when address verification fails.
laura-ops: AVS was showing 'N' on that charge (card AVS mismatch), support ticket includes note: "billing address same as org, card used by grant admin with different CC address".
fin-ellen: If AVS failed, the fallback to BIN could make us pick the BIN country/state which for that BIN maps to MA — that doesn't explain applying tax if customer is exempt. We should check exemption lookup path.
tax-bot: Automated check: exemption status on file (EX-993) is ACTIVE, verified 2025-12-20. Policy: exemptions are applied iff exemption.valid==true AND invoice.payee_entity matches exemption.entity_id. Current invoice.payee_entity: "GreenLeaf Boston Chapter". Exemption.entity_id: "GreenLeaf National". -> mismatch.
sam-support: So it's a name mismatch between chapter and national entity. Customer thought their exemption covers all chapters.
laura-ops: Quick remedy: issue a credit for the tax line and update invoice metadata to link to the verified exemption entity once customer provides signed attestation for chapter coverage.
girish-eng: For troubleshooting, repro steps for eng if you want to see the exact code path:

```
# repro locally
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/internal/invoice/2026-03-11-GL4421?expand=taxes,customer"
# then run resolver
PYTHONPATH=. python tools/tax_resolver.py --invoice 2026-03-11-GL4421 --trace
```

That will print fallback decisions and which field matched.
fin-ellen: I'll prepare a credit note draft for the full tax amount $242.30 and hold until customer confirms chapter-level coverage. Also will flag to legal for long-term policy.
sam-support: Customer replied in ticket: they can provide a chapter attestation PDF and wants the refund processed asap.
laura-ops: Action items: @fin-ellen create credit and provisional refund; @girish-eng add a debug log to show exemption.entity_id on all future tax decisions; sam-support coordinate doc upload and forward to billing.
fin-ellen: On it, will attach credit note id CN-2026-778 in the ticket once done. ETA 4 business hours.
girish-eng: I'll add the debug trace and a one-line hotfix to skip BIN fallback when an ACTIVE exemption exists for the account but entity names differ (so ops can decide). Will open PR and tag for quick deploy.
laura-ops: Thanks team. Please add a short note to the ticket explaining why it happened so customer sees we did root cause (entity mismatch + AVS fallback) :thumbsup:
sam-support: Closing loop here after credit issued. Will post update.
